summary: Adds two optional features to TWAMP. One lets the responding host return some of the command or padding octets to the sender, and the other makes test packets the same size in both directions.

eli5.summary: TWAMP tests a network by bouncing messages back and forth. This lets the returning message carry some of the original bytes and lets both directions use the same size.

subtitle: Two optional TWAMP add-ons: bounce chosen bytes back to the sender, and keep test packets the same size in both directions.

tldr.problem: Core TWAMP lets the reflector shrink its reply by truncating padding, but that is not guaranteed and is impossible when there is too little padding. Senders also have no assured way to tag a packet and get the tag back.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC assigns two new bits in the TWAMP Modes field. Reflect Octets makes the Server and Session-Reflector return designated octets, and Symmetrical Size defines a new Session-Sender packet format that already has the reflector's larger header built in.
tldr.outcome: Both features are OPTIONAL, and a system does not need them to claim compliance with RFC 5357. The RFC updates RFC 5357 and says the extensions do not appear to permit any new attacks.

today: RFC 6038 is a Proposed Standard that updates RFC 5357. It has not been obsoleted or updated by a later RFC, according to the metadata for this site.

sections.title: Why Extend TWAMP
sections.content:
The Two-Way Active Measurement Protocol (TWAMP, RFC 5357) extends the One-way Active Measurement Protocol (OWAMP, RFC 4656). Review of TWAMP produced several recommendations for new features, and this memo describes two closely related ones.

Reflect Octets is an OPTIONAL capability for the responding host to return a limited number of unassigned (padding) octets to the Control-Client or Session-Sender. The sender can embed information it finds useful and be assured that the reply will contain it.

Symmetrical Size is an OPTIONAL sender packet format that ensures test packets are the same size in both directions. TWAMP already recommends padding truncation for this, but it is not guaranteed that the reflector truncates, and it cannot work if there is not enough padding.

Measurement systems are not required to implement either feature to claim compliance with RFC 5357. Throughout, bits marked MBZ (Must Be Zero) MUST be set to zero by senders and ignored by receivers.
sections.eli5: Two extra tricks for a game where you send a message and get an echo. One lets you get your own note back. The other keeps the note and the echo the same size.

sections.title: Agreeing to Use the New Modes
sections.content:
TWAMP-Control uses the Modes field to pick communication capabilities, and that field is a recognized extension mechanism. Connection setup still follows RFC 4656 and RFC 5357, but two new bit positions are used.

The Server sets one or both of the new bits in the Modes field of its Server Greeting to show what it is willing to do. If the Control-Client wants all test sessions on this control connection to use a new mode, it MUST set the matching bit in the Setup Response message. The Client MAY set several Mode bits at once.

The Modes value the Server sends is the bit-wise OR of the modes it supports. With this memo the last 7 bit positions of the 32-bit Modes field are in use, and the other bits stay available for future extensions. Once a mode is agreed, the Control-Client, Server, Session-Sender and Session-Reflector all MUST conform to it.
sections.eli5: Before playing, each side says which special rules it knows. If both know a rule, they agree to play by it.

sections.title: Control Messages for Reflect Octets
sections.content:
The Request-TW-Session command gains two 2-octet fields after the Type-P Descriptor. Octets to be reflected holds the octets the Server MUST reflect in its Accept Session message. Length of padding to reflect is an unsigned value in octets that says how much padding the Session-Sender expects back in the test packets, so the Server can decide in advance whether it can comply.

The existing Padding Length field still gives the padding appended to ALL test packets. It SHALL be greater than the length of padding to reflect. With the recommended truncation it SHALL be at least 27 plus the reflected length in Unauthenticated mode, and at least 56 plus the reflected length in Authenticated or Encrypted modes.

The Accept Session message gains two 2-octet fields. Reflected octets carries back the requested octets. Server octets either holds information the Server wants returned in the test packets, or is all zeros if it does not need that. If the supplied padding is too short to produce equal-length packets, the Accept field MUST be set to 3, meaning some aspect of the request is not supported.
sections.eli5: When you ask to play, you hand over a small tag to be echoed back and say how much of your note should come back. The host can say yes, add its own tag, or say it cannot do that.

sections.title: What the Session-Sender Sends
sections.content:
With Reflect Octets, the test packet's padding is split. The Packet Padding (to be reflected) field has exactly the length given in Length of padding to reflect, and the rest is Additional Packet Padding. If the Server returned a non-zero Server octets value, the sender MUST place those octets in the first 2 octets of the reflected padding field.

When truncation is used, the sender MUST append enough padding to anticipate the reflector's larger header. The table in the RFC gives header sizes and the resulting truncated padding.

With Symmetrical Size, the sender uses a new Unauthenticated packet format: Sequence Number, Timestamp, Error Estimate, then MBZ (27 octets), then Packet Padding. The 27 zero octets stand in for the extra space the reflector's header will need. In Authenticated or Encrypted modes the equivalent is 56 MBZ octets. If both modes are on, the reflected padding follows the MBZ octets, before the Additional Packet Padding.
sections.eli5: The sender writes its note with some blank space reserved, so that when the host writes a longer reply header, the reply is still the same size.

sections.title: What the Session-Reflector Does
sections.content:
The reflector follows RFC 5357 with additions. In Reflect Octets mode, the designated octets from the sender's padding MUST appear in the reflector's packet, in a field called Packet Padding (from Session-Sender). If the Server gave a non-zero Server octets value, the reflector reflects it like the rest of that padding. The reflector MAY reuse other padding from the sender.

When recommended truncation is used together with Reflect Octets, the reflector MUST discard the highest-numbered octets so its packet length equals the sender's. It MUST truncate exactly 27 octets in Unauthenticated mode and exactly 56 octets in Authenticated and Encrypted modes.

In Symmetrical Size mode the reflector's packet format is unchanged from RFC 5357. Its packet length SHALL equal the sender's packet length, and it builds the packet from information in the sender's packet.
sections.eli5: The host copies back the part of your note you asked for, and trims any extra so its reply is exactly as long as yours.

sections.title: New TWAMP-Modes Registry Values
sections.content:
The memo adds two modes to the IANA TWAMP-Modes registry. Modes are indicated by setting bits in the 32-bit Modes field. The registry expects new features to get increasing values that correspond to single bit positions.

The new entries are 32 for the Reflect Octets Capability (new bit position 5) and 64 for the Symmetrical Size Sender Test Packet Format (new bit position 6).
sections.eli5: Each special rule gets its own numbered switch on a control panel, and the rule book records which switch is which.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: The RFC says these extended modes of operation do not appear to permit any new attacks on hosts communicating with core TWAMP. The security considerations that apply to any active measurement of live networks are relevant here too, and the RFC points to RFC 4656 and RFC 5357 for them.
sections.eli5: These add-ons do not seem to open any new doors for troublemakers, but the usual care for measuring real networks still applies.

items.label: Reflect Octets Capability
items.desc: New bit position 5. Server and Session-Reflector return designated octets.

items.label: Symmetrical Size Sender Test Packet Format
items.desc: New bit position 6. Sender uses the new packet format so both directions are the same size.

fields.name: Sequence Number
fields.desc: Sequence number of the test packet.

fields.name: MBZ (27 octets)
fields.desc: Zero octets that start here and run for 27 octets in total, standing in for the reflector's larger header.
